title: Shear removes obliquely laid trabeculae, leaving those aligned with stress lines

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Shear removes obliquely laid trabeculae, leaving those aligned with stress lines

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Trabecular alignment arises because a trabecula laid down along a pressure or tension line is undisturbed, since there is no shear along those lines, whereas one lying obliquely is acted on by shearing force and displaced until it comes into line with the stress.

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. XVI: On Form and Mechanical Efficiency

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: If it lie in the direction of one of the pressure-lines, for instance, it will be in a position of comparative equilibrium, or minimal disturbance; but if it be inclined obliquely to the pressure-lines, the shearing force will at once tend to act upon it and move it away.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci On Growth and Form claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: D’Arcy Wentworth Thompson, On Growth and Form (1st ed., Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1917), Chapter XVI, “On Form and Mechanical Efficiency”; topic “Trabecular architecture and stress lines”. Scope: formation of trabecular bone (and by extension fibre alignment in plants)

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on thompson1917-ch16-06: needs-new-data, resolvability 0.37

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The mechanism has measurable consequences but Thompson's “move” requires interpretive mapping to remodeling. Static scans cannot distinguish shear-driven selection from biological mechanosensing alternatives; decisive longitudinal paired data are lacking.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Track individual trabeculae longitudinally under known loading and test whether oblique elements experience greater shear and are displaced or resorbed toward principal stress directions while aligned elements persist.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Remodeling by resorption and formation is not literal mechanical displacement.

Individual-trabecula longitudinal imaging under measured loads is rare.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The claim is a process, not the finished architecture. Public micro-CT can show that trabeculae end up aligned, which several mechanisms share. A decisive test needs longitudinal imaging of the same struts under controlled shear, and that kind of open time series is not available for the analysis Thompson's wording requires.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Track individual trabeculae through time under a known shear field and record whether oblique elements are displaced into the principal-stress directions while aligned elements stay put. Support would be shear-driven relocation on that time scale; loss and replacement by cell remodeling, with no displacement of the existing strut, would fail Thompson's mechanism even if the final pattern matches the stress lines.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
In-vivo loading series that do exist are small, scattered in papers, and rarely deposit the image time series.

Static micro-CT shows the aligned end state and does not record whether shear moved the strut.
